ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: the figure shows a voltage-divider-biased NPN common-emitter amplifier. The power supply is VCC=+12 V; the base is connected to VCC by R1=33 kΩ and to ground by R2=11 kΩ to form a voltage-divider bias, and the input vi is connected to the base node through a 1 μF coupling capacitor. The collector is connected to VCC through RC=5 kΩ, and the output vo is taken from the collector through a 1 μF coupling capacitor. Below the emitter, RS=10 Ω is first connected in series, then RE=1 kΩ is connected in series to ground; the bypass capacitor CE=1 mF is connected from the connection point of RS and RE to ground, so in AC CE bypasses the 1 kΩ RE, not the 10 Ω RS. Then reason: in DC analysis all capacitors are open-circuited, and the base voltage-divider network is equivalent to a Thevenin source: Vth=12×11/(33+11)=3 V, Rth=33 kΩ || 11 kΩ=8.25 kΩ. The total DC emitter resistance is RS+RE=10+1000=1010 Ω. From the base loop, IB=(Vth−VBE)/(Rth+(β+1)(RS+RE))=(3−0.7)/(8250+201×1010)=2.3/211260=10.89 μA. Therefore IC=βIB=200×10.89 μA=2.18 mA. The small-signal parameters are gm=IC/VT=2.18 mA/25 mV=0.0871 S, r_pi=β/gm=200/0.0871≈2.30 kΩ. At AC midband, the coupling capacitors and CE are regarded as short circuits, VCC is AC ground, RE=1 kΩ is bypassed, and only RS=10 Ω remains at the emitter as an unbypassed degeneration resistor. Ignoring the Early effect and the external load, the gain from base input to collector output is Av=vo/vi=−gm RC/[1+RS(gm+1/r_pi)]. Substituting gm=0.0871 S, RC=5000 Ω, RS=10 Ω, r_pi≈2296 Ω, Av=−0.0871×5000/[1+10(0.0871+1/2296)]≈−435.5/1.875≈−232. Therefore the voltage gain is approximately −232.

method.method_draft: First describe the image as a divider-biased common-emitter BJT amplifier and note that CE bypasses the 1 kΩ emitter resistor but not the 10 Ω resistor. For DC, open all capacitors and replace R1-R2 by Vth=12·11/(33+11)=3 V and Rth=33k||11k=8.25 kΩ. Since the DC emitter resistance is Rs+RE=1010 Ω, compute IB=(Vth-0.7)/(Rth+(β+1)(1010 Ω)), then IC=βIB. Use IC and VT to find gm and r_pi. For AC midband, short the coupling capacitors and CE, so RE is at AC ground and only Rs=10 Ω remains in the emitter. Substitute gm, r_pi, and RC=5 kΩ into the hybrid-pi emitter-degenerated gain formula to obtain approximately -232.

再推理：直流分析时所有电容开路，基极分压网络等效为 Thevenin 源：Vth=12×11/(33+11)=3 V，Rth=33 kΩ || 11 kΩ=8.25 kΩ。直流发射极总电阻为 RS+RE=10+1000=1010 Ω。由基极回路得 IB=(Vth−VBE)/(Rth+(β+1)(RS+RE))=(3−0.7)/(8250+201×1010)=2.3/211260=10.89 μA。于是 IC=βIB=200×10.89 μA=2.18 mA。小信号参数为 gm=IC/VT=2.18 mA/25 mV=0.0871 S，r_pi=β/gm=200/0.0871≈2.30 kΩ。交流中频时耦合电容和 CE 视为短路，VCC 为交流地，RE=1 kΩ 被旁路，只有 RS=10 Ω 留在发射极作为未旁路退化电阻。忽略 Early 效应和外接负载，基极输入到集电极输出的增益为 Av=vo/vi=−gm RC/[1+RS(gm+1/r_pi)]。代入 gm=0.0871 S、RC=5000 Ω、RS=10 Ω、r_pi≈2296 Ω，Av=−0.0871×5000/[1+10(0.0871+1/2296)]≈−435.5/1.875≈−232。因此电压增益约为 −232。

method.method_draft: First extract the visual component placement and values, especially that CE bypasses RE=1 kΩ while Rs=10 Ω remains unbypassed. Compute the DC emitter current using the loaded divider bias: reduce R1 and R2 to Vth=3 V and Rth=8.25 kΩ, then solve IE=(β+1)(Vth−VBE)/(Rth+(β+1)(Rs+RE)). From IE, compute the intrinsic emitter resistance re=VT/IE. For the AC gain, treat the input capacitor as a short so vi is applied at the base, set VCC to AC ground, and treat CE as a short so the AC emitter resistance is only Rs=10 Ω plus re. The T-model gives ie=vi/(re+Rs), ic=αie, and v0=−icRC; evaluating this gives about -232.
method.CoT_raw:
图像描述：电路是一个共射 BJT 放大器。图中上方电源为 VCC=+12 V。基极偏置由 R1=33 kΩ 从 VCC 接到基极节点、R2=11 kΩ 从基极节点接地构成。输入 vi 通过 1 μF 耦合电容接到基极。集电极通过 RC=5 kΩ 接到 VCC，输出 vo 通过 1 μF 电容从集电极耦合出来。发射极下方先串联一个 Rs=10 Ω，再接 RE=1 kΩ 到地；旁路电容 CE=1 mF 从 Rs 与 RE 的中间节点接地，因此 CE 只旁路 RE=1 kΩ，而 Rs=10 Ω 在交流小信号中仍未被旁路。

推理计算：先对基极分压网络作戴维南等效，Vth=12×11/(33+11)=3 V，Rth=R1||R2=33 kΩ||11 kΩ=8.25 kΩ。直流时 CE 开路，所以发射极直流电阻为 Rs+RE=10 Ω+1 kΩ=1010 Ω。由加载分压偏置关系：IE=(β+1)(Vth−VBE)/(Rth+(β+1)(Rs+RE))。代入 β=200、VBE=0.7 V，IE=201×(3−0.7)/(8250+201×1010)=462.3/211260≈2.188 mA。于是小信号发射结内阻 re=VT/IE=25 mV/2.188 mA≈11.42 Ω。

交流时输入耦合电容视为短路，所以 vi 加到基极；VCC 为交流地；CE 视为短路，所以 RE 被旁路，交流发射极外接电阻只剩 Rs=10 Ω。用 T 模型，ie=vi/(re+Rs)，ic=αie，其中 α=β/(β+1)=200/201。输出在 RC 上反相，v0=−icRC，因此电压增益 Av=v0/vi=−αRC/(re+Rs)=−(200/201)×5000/(11.42+10)≈−232。

raw_record.original_question: For the amplifier shown in the figure, the BJT parameters are \(V_{BE}=0.7\,\text{V}\), \(\beta=200\), and thermal voltage \(V_T=25\,\text{mV}\). What is the voltage gain \(\left(\frac{v_0}{v_i}\right)\) of the amplifier?
raw_record.final_cot:
First describe the image: the figure shows a voltage-divider-biased NPN common-emitter amplifier. The power supply is VCC=+12 V; the base is connected to VCC by R1=33 kΩ and to ground by R2=11 kΩ to form a voltage-divider bias, and the input vi is connected to the base node through a 1 μF coupling capacitor. The collector is connected to VCC through RC=5 kΩ, and the output vo is taken from the collector through a 1 μF coupling capacitor. Below the emitter, RS=10 Ω is first connected in series, then RE=1 kΩ is connected in series to ground; the bypass capacitor CE=1 mF is connected from the connection point of RS and RE to ground, so in AC CE bypasses the 1 kΩ RE, not the 10 Ω RS.
Then reason: in DC analysis all capacitors are open-circuited, and the base voltage-divider network is equivalent to a Thevenin source: Vth=12×11/(33+11)=3 V, Rth=33 kΩ || 11 kΩ=8.25 kΩ. The total DC emitter resistance is RS+RE=10+1000=1010 Ω. From the base loop, IB=(Vth−VBE)/(Rth+(β+1)(RS+RE))=(3−0.7)/(8250+201×1010)=2.3/211260=10.89 μA. Therefore IC=βIB=200×10.89 μA=2.18 mA. The small-signal parameters are gm=IC/VT=2.18 mA/25 mV=0.0871 S, r_pi=β/gm=200/0.0871≈2.30 kΩ. At AC midband, the coupling capacitors and CE are regarded as short circuits, VCC is AC ground, RE=1 kΩ is bypassed, and only RS=10 Ω remains at the emitter as an unbypassed degeneration resistor. Ignoring the Early effect and the external load, the gain from base input to collector output is Av=vo/vi=−gm RC/[1+RS(gm+1/r_pi)]. Substituting gm=0.0871 S, RC=5000 Ω, RS=10 Ω, r_pi≈2296 Ω, Av=−0.0871×5000/[1+10(0.0871+1/2296)]≈−435.5/1.875≈−232. Therefore the voltage gain is approximately −232.
